Mel, thanks for the tag Lou. Usual disclaimer that I haven't seen your leg so I can't diagnose it over the internet. But morning stiffness and a sore spot a few cm up from the heel after a big jump in k's is the classic pattern for a mid-portion Achilles tendinopathy, not a tear. It's a load problem, so the fix is managing the load, not resting it completely.

Running: you don't usually have to stop. Drop back to around what you were doing before the jump, keep it flat and easy, and let the pain rule below decide how much.

Strength: heel drops off a step are fine, but heavy slow calf raises have better evidence these days. Something like 3-4 sets of 6-8, three seconds up and three seconds down, about three times a week, adding weight as it gets easier. On the bad days swap them for isometric holds: up on your toes, hold 30-45 seconds, 4 or 5 times.

Pain: up to about 3/10 while you're loading it is ok, as long as it's settled by the next morning. If it's worse the next morning you did too much, so back it off a notch. Limping round the office after the 6k suggests that one was a bit much.

What I'd steer clear of: hard stretching, which tends to stir up an irritable tendon, and cortisone anywhere near the Achilles. It can feel better short term but it's not kind to the tendon itself. So you can skip the needle.

If it's not settling in 3-4 weeks, see a sports physio. Any one near you in Bayswater will do.

One thing to act on straight away: a sudden pop, a feeling like you've been kicked in the back of the leg, or not being able to push off. If that happens, stop running and the calf work and get it checked urgently that day, GP or ED, because it could be a rupture. Also worth knowing that some antibiotics can make tendons more vulnerable, so if you've been on any lately, mention it to whoever looks at it.
